concepts.title: Fashion Terminology: Fashion, Style, Fad, Classic
concepts.definition: Fashion names the styles most popular at a given moment; a style is any distinct look that survives even after leaving fashion; fads burn out within a season for want of design strength; classics such as blazers and polo shirts stay accepted for years through sheer simplicity.
concepts.formula: life span ladder -- fad to fashion to classic
concepts.key_idea: A style never dies, it only steps out of fashion; simplicity is what keeps a classic from dating.
question_patterns: define fashion and style and distinguish between them
what is a fad and give two examples
which qualities keep a classic from becoming obsolete
why do fads fail to hold consumer attention
place hot pants, a blazer jacket and this season's print into fashion terms

solution_steps.explain: popularity now, permanent look, one season wonder, long acceptance
baggy pants are fads, the Chanel suit is a classic

worked_examples.q: Which look burns out within a season: a fad or a classic?

concepts.title: Historic Growth of Fashion
concepts.definition: Fashion as change is young: styles froze for a century until the Renaissance, Paris rose through the royal court and the silk trade with couture dressmaking, the Industrial Revolution and the sewing machine democratised clothing, Levi Strauss turned tent cloth into work denims, the 1880s gave women separates, ready to wear arrived in 1920 and Yves Saint Laurent launched the first full pret a porter line in the 1960s.
concepts.formula: timeline -- court couture to machine made to ready to wear
concepts.key_idea: The sewing machine turned a handcraft into an industry and opened fashion to the middle class.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe202.txt, Fashion Development and France sections (approx lines 94-154)

solution_steps.explain: Renaissance quickening, French court, industrial machines, denims, separates, ready to wear
each step widened who could afford fashion

worked_examples.q: Which machine turned clothing from handcraft into industry: the sewing machine or the loom?

concepts.title: Stages of the Fashion Cycle
concepts.definition: A style travels a bell shaped curve of acceptance measured in sales: designers introduce it, popularity rises, it peaks with mass copies at many price levels, declines onto sale racks as copies saturate taste, and ends in rejection when buyers move to the next new look.
concepts.formula: cycle stages -- introduction plus rise plus peak plus decline plus rejection
concepts.key_idea: Heavy copying is the very thing that tires fashion leaders and pushes the curve downward.
question_patterns: name and explain the stages of the fashion cycle
what shape does the fashion cycle take and what does its height measure

how does mass copying push a style into decline

solution_steps.explain: from designer debut to consumer abandonment
acceptance is plotted as sales volume over time

worked_examples.q: Name the fashion cycle's first stage: introduction or rejection?

concepts.title: Fashion Merchandising and the Six Rights
concepts.definition: Fashion merchandising is the planning that puts the wanted goods in the wanted place at the wanted time, in the wanted quantity, at a price that pays the store yet meets competition, backed by promotion worth its cost -- the recipe for maximum profit.
concepts.formula: merchandising = right merchandise plus place plus time plus quantity plus price plus promotion
concepts.key_idea: The merchandiser converts inspiration into design and steers planning, production, promotion and distribution toward consumer demand.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe202.txt, merchandising definition and rights (approx lines 215-223, 339-352)
question_patterns: what do you understand by fashion merchandising

solution_steps.explain: planning across merchandise, place, time, quantity, price, promotion
customer demand, accessibility, season, inventory balance, profit with competition, promotion appeal

worked_examples.q: Planning that puts the wanted goods in the wanted place at the wanted time is called fashion what: merchandising or mounting?

concepts.title: Roles of the Merchandiser: Make, Buy, Promote, Sell
concepts.definition: In manufacturing the merchandiser advises on fabrics and finds the best production route for the price and target market; in buying, trend analysis sharpens ordering; in promotion, fashion shows and visual skill court bulk buyers; in selling, display suggestions and market reading close the loop with stores.
concepts.formula: role chain -- manufacture plus buy plus promote plus sell
concepts.key_idea: Historical and socio-cultural knowledge of fabrics is what lets a merchandiser turn a designer's vision into a salable product.
question_patterns: describe the merchandiser's role in manufacturing
how does trend forecasting improve buying decisions
how does a merchandiser promote a designer's product
what responsibilities come with selling fashion items to stores
why must a merchandiser understand fabric construction

solution_steps.explain: fabric input and production choices, informed ordering, buyer facing promotion, store facing sales
textiles, forecasting, target market sense and communication

worked_examples.q: In manufacturing, the merchandiser advises on which inputs: fabrics or weather?

concepts.title: Levels of Merchandising
concepts.definition: Merchandising operates at three levels: inside retail organisations where internal planning stocks the sales floor profitably, through buying agencies that procure, negotiate, and police quality for clients, and inside export houses where buyer merchandisers link client to factory while production merchandisers keep output on schedule.
concepts.formula: levels -- retail organisation plus buying agency plus export house
concepts.key_idea: Buying agencies save exporters cost and time; in export houses the buyer side sources and samples while the production side delivers on time.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe202.txt, three levels of merchandising (approx lines 271-307)
question_patterns: describe the three levels of merchandising

solution_steps.explain: store internal planning, procurement office, export house bridge
buyer link for sourcing and sampling, production link for schedules

worked_examples.q: At which level does internal planning stock the sales floor: retail organisations or export houses?

concepts.title: Target Market and Market Segmentation
concepts.definition: A target market is the consumer category likeliest to buy the offering, found by segmenting the whole market into subsets that share needs -- by demography such as age, sex, income, by geography and climate, by psychographic lifestyle, or by behavioural opinion and usage of products.
concepts.formula: segmentation bases -- demographic plus geographic plus psychographic plus behavioural
concepts.key_idea: Segmentation concentrates sales effort where returns are highest and reads the motivations behind buying.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe202.txt, target market and segmentation (approx lines 310-334)

solution_steps.explain: the likeliest buyers worth focusing sales spending on
population traits, place and climate, lifestyle, product opinions

worked_examples.q: The consumer category likeliest to buy the offering is the target what: market or mall?

concepts.title: Fashion Retail Organisations
concepts.definition: Retail formats run from the owner run neighbourhood single unit store through department stores with separate sections to chain stores sharing one brand and central management; inside large stores the work splits into merchandising, sales promotion, finance and control, operations, and personnel or branch divisions.
concepts.formula: formats -- single unit plus department plus chain; divisions -- merchandise plus promotion plus finance plus operations plus personnel
concepts.key_idea: Organisational structure shifts with merchandise type, firm size and target customer.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe202.txt, retail organisations and divisions (approx lines 353-408)
question_patterns: compare small single unit stores, department stores and chain stores

solution_steps.explain: family run single store, sectioned department store, standardised chain
buying and selling, promotion, finance, operations, personnel

worked_examples.q: Which store format shares one brand and central management: chain stores or single units?

concepts.title: Skills, Courses and Careers in Fashion
concepts.section: Preparing for a Career and Scope
concepts.definition: Success needs three divergent abilities -- forecasting trends ahead of time, analysing the dollars and sense of styles against company and consumer budgets, and communicating well enough to negotiate, sell and write copy; training runs from six month certificates through two year master's to four year bachelor's programmes, leading to work as visual merchandise designer, fashion designer, set designer or interior designer.
concepts.formula: skill triad -- forecasting plus analytical plus communication
concepts.key_idea: About one third of professional fashion designers are self employed, and most aspirants specialise in one area such as apparel, displays or theatre sets.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe202.txt, career preparation and scope (approx lines 409-526)
question_patterns: which three skills must a fashion merchandiser possess

solution_steps.explain: reading trends early, juggling costs and budgets, negotiating and writing
certificate to bachelor's; window displays to film sets to interiors

worked_examples.q: About what share of professional fashion designers are self-employed: one third or one hundredth?

concepts.title: Croquis Height Arithmetic
concepts.section: Practical 1: developing a female fashion figure
concepts.definition: A fashion croquis is drawn in head units, so the height of the sketch on paper is the number of heads multiplied by the chosen head length in inches.
concepts.key_idea: Fashion figures run eight and a half to ten heads tall, with the centre front line divided into that many equal parts.
question_patterns: a croquis is drawn 10 heads tall with each head measuring 1 inch; how tall is the sketch in inches
a fashion figure of 8.5 heads is drawn with 2 inch heads; compute the height of the drawing
find the paper height of a croquis from its head count and head size
a student draws a 10 head figure with 1.5 inch heads; how many inches long is the centre front line
calculate the drawn height when the head unit and the number of heads are stated

solution_steps.action: multiply head count by head size
solution_steps.explain: the head is the unit of measurement, so heads times head length gives the figure height

worked_examples.q: Fashion figures run eight and a half to how many heads tall: ten or two?

concepts.title: Study Programme Duration Gaps
concepts.definition: Fashion education routes differ in length -- certificates and diplomas finish in six months to a year, master's degrees take two years and bachelor's four -- so the extra years one route demands over another is simply the longer duration minus the shorter.
concepts.key_idea: Choosing a bachelor's over a one year diploma means investing three extra years for broader promotion chances.
question_patterns: a bachelor's in fashion merchandising takes 4 years and a diploma takes 1 year; how many extra years does the degree demand
find the gap in years between two study routes when both durations are stated
a master's programme runs 2 years against a 1 year certificate; compute the difference
how much longer is a 4 year bachelor's than a 2 year master's in this field
calculate the additional years of schooling one route needs over another

solution_steps.explain: the difference between the two routes is the extra investment

worked_examples.q: A master's degree in fashion takes how many years: two or twenty?

concepts.title: Self-Employment Share of Designers
concepts.definition: When a stated fraction of a designer population works for itself, applying that fraction to the total gives the number of independent professionals -- about one third in fashion design.
concepts.key_idea: Roughly one in three professional fashion designers runs an independent practice, which fuels the field's entrepreneurial appeal.
question_patterns: one third of a city's 900 professional fashion designers are self employed; how many run their own practice

a design association has 4500 members and one third are freelancers; find the freelancer count
calculate the self employed designers when the total and the independent fraction are given
how many of 600 designers would be self employed at a one third rate

solution_steps.action: apply the fraction to the total
solution_steps.explain: multiply the designer count by the self employment share

worked_examples.q: About one in how many professional fashion designers is self-employed: three or thirty?
